articleTitle: Calculation of Radio Signal Attenuation Using Annual Precipitation and Heavy Rainfall Data
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The empirical Chebil's model was used to calculate the rain rate value. According to the peculiarities of climatic conditions of Lithuania the change in this model was made. Obtained values of rain rate for the investigated localities of Lithuania were compared with ones calculated using Rice-Holmberg method and with the ITU-R (International Telecommunication Union-Radio Regulations) value. Analysis of these values and meteorological data of Lithuania has shown the necessity to specify rain zone ascription. The values of rain attenuation have been calculated as well.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Modelling of Semi-Anechoic Chamber between 30 and 200 MHz
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The EMI performance of a semi-anechoic chamber can be deduced from the difference between attenuation in an open area test site (OATS), called Normalized Site Attenuation (NSA) and this same measure in the test chamber (fig. 1). The EN50147-2 standard [1] authorizes a maximum deviation of 4dB. Numerical modelling enables us to know and thus optimise chamber performance. In this work, we propose a new boundary condition for modelling the reflectivity of ferrite tile and an antenna modelling. to take into account the important mutual coupling effect in the 30 to 200 MHz band unlike other interesting works [2,3,4] which consider electrically small antennas.

articleTitle: Discussion of Measuring Methods and Suggested Measurements Systems to Determine Magnetic and RF Fields from MRI Equipment
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Magnetic and RF fields with complex characteristics surround MRI systems. A comprehensive method for the determination of such fields and authors’ systems to measure them is described. Results of determinations are discussed.

articleTitle: Practical Radio Noise Measurements
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This document describes a frequency independent method for measuring radio noise in practical radio applications. It is addressed to radio and radiomonitoring engineers, frequency planners and other parties using actual radio noise data.

articleTitle: Monte-Carlo Modelling of Co-Existence of Radio Systems Using Smart Antennas or Dynamic Frequency Selection
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents possibilities of modelling the radio interference and co-existence of novel radiocommunications systems that employ Smart Antenna or Dynamic Frequency Selection (DFS) technologies. The Monte-Carlo approach is used here by means of employing an open SEAMCAT software tool, distributed publicly by ERO.

articleTitle: Rail Circuit in the Condition of Electromagnetic Influence of Traction Net
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with the determination of spectrum composition of traction current at the a. c. and d. c. traction. The most dangerous interferences are 50, 75 and 100 Hz harmonics for normal work of rail circuits at the d. c. traction. The harmonics, coinciding with the code frequency (25 Hz), are inadmissible for the rail circuits of railway section at the a. c. traction. The station rail circuits are protected from interference well enough.

articleTitle: Coexistence Problems between GSM900 and CDMA2000 Networks in Poland
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents some problems connected with the coexistence of the GSM900 and CDMA2000 systems in Poland. It corrects the approach proposed in the ECC document [1] and shows the difficulties with the measurement of CDMA/GSM base stations and with development of the method of calculating the separation distance between both systems.

articleTitle: The Separation of Tasks between Radio Communications Regulators
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Although economic, legal and technical rules for telecommunications market liberalization have raised a great interest, the institutional framework where those rules take place was neglected. Many European countries have decided to divide regulatory powers between two different actors: a national regulatory agency and the Telecommunication minister. The problem relies upon the fact that both authorities have sufficient responsibilities and discretion to reach private objectives that can lead to a conflict of interest between the two regulators. In this paper, we report and research an extreme such a case that recently happened in Republic of Serbia. Namely, as soon as the new national telecommunication regulator has been established with great responsibilities the Ministry has taken back most of its regulatory power by a decree. We discuss the reasons behind the decision, consequences especially in spectrum management and proper actions to be taken to remedy obvious regulatory inefficiency.

articleTitle: GTEM Cell Characterization and Application above 1 GHz
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Based on EN 61000-4-20 EMI and susceptibility measurements in GTEM cells become more and more important because of a less time consuming procedure, and the experiences gained over the last decade. Different methods to characterize GTEM cell properties (1250 mm height of septum) have been studied. Results presented show an acceptable good consistence among one other and with results reported by other authors

articleTitle: Characteristics of Parametrically Amplifying Trvelling-Wave Antennas Somewhat Analogous to Travelling Tubes and Esaki Diode and Possible Applicatios to Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: While the conventional Beverage Antenna is based on ground return at low frequencies, theory and experiment of propagation along a wire above ground was extended to high frequencies. Attenuation characteristics possess a maximum and a minimum and the wave-mode becomes a hybrid fast wave in the transition region. This has led to an invention of parametrically amplifying antennas and summarizes its function and recognized to be somewhat analogous to traveling wave tubes and the Esaki diode. Possible applications to satellite communications for high gain and directivity reception

articleTitle: Powerline Communication - Just Another Communication Technology or an Electromagnetic Disaster?
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The EMC of Powerline Communications (PLC) is discussed in many standardization working groups and on congresses and symposia. Often models developed some tens of years ago are used to investigate the disturbance potential of the PLC modems. In this paper investigation methods are presented, which are based directly on the basic interference model with a radio receiver like device as susceptible device. Results of comparison measurements with other wired IT systems are shown.

articleTitle: Parameter Study of Transmitter Antenna and Balun for Anechoic Chamber
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The electric field strength within an anechoic chamber is dependent on the antenna characteristics, sparameters, standing wave ratio (SWR), dimensions of the chamber and the power of the RF amplifier. If the antenna and the s-parameters are optimized, it is possible to produce the required electromagnetic field with less power. The following paper illustrates a new broad band antenna using different baluns, i.e. baluns with ring core and baluns with coax cable. A parameter study has been done by conducting various experiments. A simulation of the measured results is also given. For the simulation, the computer program SuperNEC is used.

articleTitle: Solution for Integro-Differential Equation of Chasmas
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Ionising beams may create a “quasi nonneutral plasma” or chasma in special circumstances. The Poisson equation leads to a non-linear integro-differential equation containing a singularity. Nevertheless the solution yields simply a constant ion density for a homogeneous beam and homogeneous ion production. In view of a recent alternative approach to study chasmas we develop here a solution method for the general situation of inhomogeneous beam and production.

articleTitle: Dynamic Frequency Selection: A Look at a Cognitive Radio Technique for the 5 Ghz Band
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper takes a look at operation in the 5 GHz band and the use of Dynamic Frequency Selection as a Cognitive Radio feature to share the band. In the U.S, there is a lot of interest of using Cognitive type radio features that will help facilitate the sharing of bands between various services. This paper discusses the 5GHz requirement that RLAN systems must use specific types of operational techniques such as TPC and DFS in order to share the band with other services such as radiolocation.

articleTitle: EMC Aware Circuit Design and Optimizations
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper describes the procedure for optimizations of integrated circuits (ICs) with respect to electromagnetic compatibility (EMC). The optimization is performed in order to reduce electromagnetic emissions and to improve electromagnetic immunity. The circuits are optimized by using the optimization approach with the cost function calculated by circuit simulations. The hybrid approach to optimization combines the global search strategy using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Direct Pattern Search (DPS) method used as local search strategy. The design of EM compatible ICs can be substantially simplified and automated by using this procedure.

articleTitle: Method of Crosstalk Reduction in a Multiconductor Telecommunication Cable
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents a method of crosstalk reduction in a screened telecommunication cable composed of four conductors. Initially, an electromagnetic and topologic code is implemented to simulate the multi conductor transmission line loaded on a specific termination network. Then, the far end crosstalk voltage is determined and injected on a real line transmitting ADSL2+ signal. With such method, it appears that is possible to decrease the crosstalk on the line for a typical configuration of source and resistor networks, and consequently to increase the bit rate level and reach of the ADSL2+ transmission.

articleTitle: Improvement of Efficiency of Hybrid Method of Moments/Finite-Difference Time-Domain Technique
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper a hybrid technique linking the frequency-domain Method of Moments and the Finite Difference Time Domain method is presented. Proposed technique is a very powerful and efficient method for analyzing complex electromagnetic problems involving perfectly conducting antennas radiating in the presence of inhomogeneous dielectric bodies of an arbitrary shape. To shorten the time of computation two techniques, based on tapering and interpolating of incident field in FDTD region, are implemented. Numerical results validating the hybrid method and showing its capabilities are also presented.

articleTitle: Radio Applications for Meteorology
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Radio-frequencies represent scarce and key resources for the meteorological community. Under the increasing demand and pressure on radio-spectrum for telecommunications or mass market applications, the related frequency bands are steadily under threat that could put at risk the whole meteorological process. In particular, satellite passive sensing, to which can mainly be attributed impressive progress made in the recent years in weather and climate analysis, are a unique natural resource and are by far the most sensible to interference. A better understanding of the scientific and meteorological use of the spectrum by other radio users and regulators would provide relevant justification that frequency bands used for meteorology need to be safeguarded collectively.

articleTitle: Activities Related to the Regional Radiocommunication Conference 2006 (RRC-06)
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Following the decision of the ITU (International Telecommunications Union), a Regional Radiocommunication Conference (RRC) took place in Geneva from 15<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> of May 2006 till the 16<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> of June 2006. The aim of this Conference was to facilitate the deployment of digital television and digital audio systems by developing a plan that will identify frequencies for a proper use of these systems. This paper provides updated information on the work relating to the development of the plan for RRC-06.

articleTitle: Mobile Phone Radiation Hazard
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper the absorption mechanism in the human tissue for mobile phones equipped with different antennas is analyzed by means of numerical simulations based on the FDTD (Finite Difference Time Domain) method. The single- or double-band antennas for 900 and 1800 MHz are situated on realistic models of mobile phones. The near E-field distribution was observed in free space and a SAR (Specific Absorption Rate) - in a semi-sphere head model and folded box hand model, filled with the tissue simulating material are observed when the handset was situated close to them. It is shown that there is a strong effect of the antenna type on both the E-field and a SAR distribution in the phantom.

articleTitle: New Approaches for Regulating International Radiocommunications
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The “Red Books” incorporates the Radio Regulations (treaty status) and decisions of the World Radiocommunication Conferences, including Resolutions, Recommendations and ITU-R Recommendations incorporated by reference.

articleTitle: Spectrum Management of Inmarsat Mobile Satellite Networks
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The demand for radio frequency spectrum for mobile satellite services in 1-3 GHz band is increasing rapidly with the introduction of advanced technologies like packet switching. In this contribution, a brief history of the evolution of mobile satellite service spectrum allocations in 1-3 GHz frequency band over several World Radio Conferences of International Telecommunication Union is presented. Background information of Inmarsat, one of the leading providers of Mobile Satellite Services in 1.5/1.6 GHz band is given. Finally, the essential elements involved in the spectrum management of INMARSAT satellite networks are described.

articleTitle: Open Questions in Relation to Power Line Communications and EMC
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper discuss the open questions still being discussed in relation to the implementation of Power Line Communications Systems (PLC) and the Electromagnetic Compatibility with other telecommunications systems including radio based systems. These questions are very much related to the EMC standards being under development in several organizations.

articleTitle: UWB Emissions and EMC
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) with ultra-wideband (UWB) signals is still controversial, with some spectrum users desiring to limit the emissions to levels below the natural microwave emissions from a human body. Here, as an example, UWB emissions at the full US indoor EIRP limit of -53.3 dBm/MHz in the 1.7-1.9 GHz bands are used to illustrate EMC with mobile phones to within a fraction of a meter separation. Also, the practical limits (-70 and -85 dBm/MHz) of emission measurements are shown in relation to US limits, and to naturally occurring microwave radiation.

articleTitle: 12GHz Realtime Measurement of Voltage and Current Transition Duration Due to Micro Gap Discharge as Low Voltage ESD
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The voltage and current transition durations due to small gap discharge as the low voltage ESD was investigated in time domain. The measurement system was set up a very wide band experimental system using the distributed constant line and coaxial electrode. The insertion loss of the experimental system was within - 3dB in frequency range below 12GHz. It was confirmed that the distributed constant experimental system enables to measure the very fast transients of about 40 ps in 12GHz bandwidth. As a consequence of the experiment using the system, voltage and current rise time of transition duration were shown 40 ps or less. Besides, the rise times were changed in configuration of electrodes, source polarity and discharging voltage.

articleTitle: Some Unresolved Issues Concerning EMC in Powerline Communications
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Some PLC technology problems whose solution is still unresolved are addressed. Regarding emissions, the need to improve our understanding of the factors influencing the k factor and the conversion between the differential and the common mode are discussed. The challenges to be met by new and existing radiation mitigation techniques are presented. The requirements of PLC channel models and simulators beyond those already available are discussed. The need for field to transmission line coupling models adapted to the complex nonuniformities of the PLC channel is stressed.

articleTitle: Analysis of Coplanar-Type Printed Lines Including Parasitic Effects of Bonding Wires between Ground Conductors
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Analysis, taking into account influence of parasitic effects of bonding wires between ground conductors on electrical characteristics of the coplanar- type lines has been worked out and employed for propagation modelling of square-wave signals along coupled coplanar waveguides (C-CPW) and coupled coplanar waveguides with grounded centre strip (C-CPWGS). Numerical results checked against TDR/TDT measurements have proven usefulness of implemented technique.

articleTitle: Stable and Effective Full-Wave PEEC Model Based on Recursive Convolution Macromodeling
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A novel technique for time domain PEEC modeling is presented. The PEEC method is a well- known numerical method for creating full-wave models of interconnection structures in frequency and time domain being in use for modeling in EMC problems. The time domain solutions by PEEC can show so-called late time instabilities. Several attempts to correct this problem have been made in the literature. The cause for instability has been reveled and a time model has been given in one of our papers. Such a model based on macromodeling is stable but ineffective concerning the simulation time. Now we present a stable full- wave PEEC model based on the recursive convolution macromodeling with a good numerical performance.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility Estimation Technique for Sharing between Fixed Wireless Access Systems and Fixed Satellite Systems in the 5725-5825 MHz Band.
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In given article the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) estimation technique for sharing between fixed wireless access systems and receivers of geostationary orbit (GSO) space stations in the 57255825 MHz band is presented. This technique was applied for EMC calculations and interferences level dependence from a satellite receiver orbit position was recognized

articleTitle: On the Outcome of ITU-R Task Group 1/8 on Ultra-Wideband Technology
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: There are several challenges associated with the introduction and use of wireless devices using ultrawideband (UWB) technology. Some of these challenges are relevant to UWB compatibility with systems operating within radiocommunication services, the development of an appropriate framework for the introduction of UWB devices, the definitions and characteristics of UWB technology and devices, and the measurement of emission levels from UWB devices. The Radiocommunication Sector of the International Telecommunications Union (ITU-R) established Task Group 1/8 (TG 1/8) to address these challenges. TG 1/8 met six times (2003 - 2005) and developed 5 documents on wireless UWB applications. This paper describes the mandate and structure of TG 1/8, the 4 draft new Recommendations and the draft new Report developed by TG 1/8, and relevant UWB developments within the ITU-R. This paper also summarizes the current trends in UWB regulations based on UWB rules adopted by some countries.

articleTitle: Distribution of Harmonics of Return Traction Current on Feeder Zone and Evaluation of its Influence on the Work of Rail Circuits
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It is proposed mathematical model, allowing us to calculate voltage and current distribution along rail net and catenary for all harmonics of traction current at the different isolation resistance. The results of modeling are done for homogenous traction net. The dangerous harmonics of traction current are 50 and 100 Hz, exceeding on a value half of minimal amplitude of a code current, for normal work of rail circuits.

Author Keywords: Distribution of harmonics of traction current

articleTitle: Numerical Simulations and the Practical Problem of Uncertainty with Regard to Material Parameters
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Numerical simulations represent a powerful tool for the investigation of electromagnetic interference situations. Their application is particularly desirable for the solution of practical problems because of the manifold advantages connected to simulations. However, in many cases these advantages only exist when the interference situation can be described very accurately regarding for example the boundary conditions, the physical arrangement or the characteristics of the structure under consideration. Then the results of numerical simulations can be taken to conclude on consequences such as mitigation measures. Material parameters are often an important input for the description of a structure and their knowledge is especially required when they affect electromagnetic phenomena in a decisive extent. On the other hand, however, such material parameters are often not known or very difficult to be determined. The paper describes the situation regarding the uncertainty of material parameters and shows the consequences for a practical case. An example is given how to overcome such deficiencies.

articleTitle: Transfer Impedance Model of Measurement Path for ESD Simulator Calibration
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with deriving a frequency dependent transfer impedance of a measurement path for calibration of an electrostatic discharge (ESD) simulator. The transfer impedance is derived from the scattering parameters of the calibration system components, i.e. the Pellegrini target, the cable with attenuator and the broadband oscilloscope, measured in the range from 1MHz to 6GHz. The frequency analysis of the whole path reveals high frequency effects neglected by the simple resistance models and makes possible reduction of the calibration uncertainty.

articleTitle: Correlation of Characteristics of Currents and Electromagnetic Fields Generated by Lightning Return Strokes to the CN Tower
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Simultaneous measurements of the return- stroke lighting current derivative at the CN Tower and the lightning generated electromagnetic pulse at a distance of 2 km north of the tower have been performed since 1991 using broadband high-resolution measurement systems. The recent installation of global positioning system (GPS) units for time synchronization of CN Tower lightning measurement stations has enabled the correlation of the characteristics of the return-stroke current, measured at the tower, with the characteristics of its generated electromagnetic field, measured 2 km north of the tower. The characteristics of the CN Tower lightning-generated electric and magnetic fields were also correlated. In this paper, the current and field analysis is based on the 2005 CN Tower lightning return-stroke data. Excellent and strong linear correlation was established between the magnetic field peak and the current peak. However, only a weak correlation was found between the magnetic field peak and the peak of the current derivative. The risetime of the electromagnetic pulse was also correlated to the current risetime. It is hoped that this paper will not only help in the establishment of simple return-stroke models at elevated structures, but also contributes to the inverse problem where lightning currents are to be estimated from field data. The obtained results are especially relevant to lightning occurring at tall structures or in mountainous areas.

articleTitle: Application of Field Simulation to a Hybrid Tem Cell: New Tools for Old Systems
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Research into electromagnetic field behaviour in TEM cells remains relevant. An understanding of field distributions and higher order resonance mechanisms will aid development of a combined TEM-reverberation immunity test facility. Prior research on the subject, for example [1], was based on a hardware experiment of a scale model facility. Application of numerical simulation to TEM and reverberation facilities allows easy exploration of different chamber layouts and injection mechanisms, and rapid analysis of system surface currents and impedances.

articleTitle: Specific Absorption Rate Calculation in Human Head Due to Hand-Held Phone Using Hybrid Mom-FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, the results of calculations of specific absorption rate inside human head using hybrid method of moments - finite difference time-domain method are presented. The analysis has been performed for frequency of 900 MHz using a heterogenous model of human head and three models of phone equipped with monopole, helical or PIFA antenna. Two positions of mobile phone has been considered. The results are related to ICNIRP guidelines and IEEE standards.

articleTitle: Uncertainty by Determination of Coil Factor According to IEC 61000-4-8
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Instead of uncertainty of field probe and ampere meter, sensitivity of measured field on deviation from central positioning in coil is dominant. Authors incorporate this sensitivity by establishing uncertainty budget by determining coil factor.

articleTitle: Regulatory Aspects: New EMC Directive
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The concerns regulatory aspects of electromagnetic compatibility. Nowadays in force is EMC Directive 89/336/EEC. In 2004 for improving legal security through a clearer and more precise text giving an answer to divergent interpretation of the 89/336/EEC directive it was taken place conception of new EMC directive 2004/108/EC.

articleTitle: Shielding Effect of Current Transformers Used in Electronic Electrical Energy Meters from Impact of External NdFeb Magnets
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Strong permanent magnets used in a wrong way can induce potentially harmful changes in the already optimised technical equipment. The watt-hour meters under strong external magnetic field do not count correctly the consumption of electrical energy.

articleTitle: Simulation of Inverter as EMI Source Considering Mains Impedance
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper inverter simulation as electromagnetic interference (EMI) source is provided considering the internal mains impedance. Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) is provided by setting of the energy charge/discharge capacitor at inverter's input and RFI filter.

articleTitle: Measurement Verification of Transmitting Antenna Modeling in the Vicinity of a Signaling Cable
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with a coupling problem of a radiating antenna placed close to a signaling cable. This aspect is examined within frames of COST 286 Joint Technical Action dedicated to interference influence of GSM phones on cabling systems of vehicles. The phenomenon is studied for various lengths of the cable, for different distance between the cable and a metal part of a vehicle and for different positions of the antenna. First phase simulations that were performed by three separate groups of researches have given results that are in very good agreement. Measurement verification of modeling procedures has been accomplished conforming simulation results. Two more aspects need to be studied yet: enclosure problems with resonances and then cumulative effects of several sources.

articleTitle: Application of Wavelet Transform for Reduction of Noise in Impulse UWB Signals
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with the method for reduction of noise and interference in UWB (Ultra wideband) impulse signals. The method, based on wavelet transform, consists in decomposition of the signal, modification of its wavelet transform coefficients and signal reconstruction. In the paper brief description of the proposed method is followed by presentation of test results and their discussion.

articleTitle: A Look at Spectrum Management in the Home
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper gives a high level overview of spectrum management issues in the home. Using the 2.4GHz band as an example, the paper briefly describes where a user can and cannot get more additional information as they deploy various wireless and non wireless devices in the house that operate in the same band.

articleTitle: Ionospheric Precursors Observed during the Mediterranean Region Earthquakes
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper investigates the features of pre-earthquake ionospheric anomalies in the total electron content (TEC) obtained on the basis of regular GPS observations at the IGS network.

Author Keywords: total electron content of the ionosphere

articleTitle: Influence of Workpieces and Machine Body on Magnetic Fields in the Surrounding of Resistance Welding Machines
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper illustrates the focusing effect of ferromagnetic workpieces and the machine bodies of resistance welding machines on the magnetic field existing in the surrounding of these machines. The investigations comprise finite element (FEM) simulations and reference measurements. For FEM calculations magnetic material properties are taken into account. Existing consequences of variations of the arrangement on the field exposure of the operators are discussed.

articleTitle: Occurence of Phase Fluctuations of GPS Signals in Antarctic Ionosphere during Severe November 2004 Storm
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents an analyze on the occurrence of strong phase fluctuations of GPS signals observed at Antarctic stations. The fluctuations caused large scales ionospheric irregularities which were associated with the occurrence of polar patches in TEC.

articleTitle: The Analysis of Electromagnetic Interferences in Cardiac Pacemakers at Occupational Environment
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents problems connected with cardiac pacemaker exposed to electromagnetic field at workplace. The authors have focused on two kinds of sources: 50/60 Hz (overhead power lines) and 10-100 MHz (dielectric sealers, medical equipments).

articleTitle: Analysis of Location Characteristics of the USA HF Spectrum Monitoring Network Using New Software
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: New software for determination of characteristics of HF direction finder networks, related to location of emission sources by triangulation, is described. Practical implementation of the software is demonstrated by calculation of location characteristics of the USA HF monitoring network under different HF propagation conditions. An example of this particular network is used to demonstrate capabilities of the new methodology in optimization of monitoring networks in the HF frequency range.

articleTitle: FDTD Modeling of Air Discharge from An ESD-Gun
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The electromagnetic noise caused by an electrostatic discharge (ESD) is a major source of malfunction to high-tech equipment. The ESD immunity testing has been prescribed in the IEC61000-4-2, which specifies the current waveform due to contact discharge from an ESD-gun through an IEC recommended current detector (Pellegrini calibration target). For air discharge from the ESD-gun, however, the IEC standard does not almost show the detailed specification due to poor reproducibility of the resultant discharge current, although this testing faithfully simulates an actual ESD event. In this paper, based on a combination of our previously developed ESD-gun model and a spark-resistance formula, we have proposed an FDTD modeling of air discharge from an ESD-gun. The effectiveness of our proposal has been demonstrated by comparing with experimental results with a 6-GHz digital oscilloscope.

articleTitle: Standardization and Regulatory Approaches Related to Radiat Emission Limits for Power Line Communications
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The developing of standards for products and networks used for power line communications (PLC) remains one of the main issues connected with this new technology. Due to the difficulty to achieve consensus for limits not much progress was achieved during the last two years. However, the Regulatory Authorities in US as well as in Europe have recognized the role which this technique can play in increasing the competition among telecommunication providers. The paper will present the state of art in the development of standards, the Regulatory environment and an overview of the PLC deployment in different parts of the world.

articleTitle: HAARP - The Research Ionosphere Station or the Ultimate Weapon of the Conspiracy
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents applications, structure, main characteristics and EMC analysis of broadband ionosphere station HAARP. The fundamental goal of this investigation is to explore and understand natural phenomena occurring in the Earth's ionosphere and near-space environment. There are contradictory information about civil and military applications, EM hazard and interference threat of the powerful ionosphere stations. Structure and parameters of the antenna array, antenna broadband matching and radiation computer modeling of the station are described.

articleTitle: Aspects of Radiated Emission Tests on Big Machines
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this article the electromagnetic radiation from large EUTs like big machines is investigated. The aim of the research is to find out how many observation points have to be chosen around the EUT in order to ensure that the maximum emission level, within a certain margin, is detected. Observation points are positioned on a hemisphere around the EUT and are equally distributed. This is an improvement compared to the procedure of CISPR16 [1], the most commonly used emission standard, where the radiation in upward direction is disregarded. The emission levels calculated for the hemisphere around the EUT are compared with values obtained according to the CISPR 16 procedure for several radiators. Ground reflections are taken into account in the simulations.

articleTitle: EMC Defect in Watt-Hour Meter (Ferraris) Operating in Strong, Stationary Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Influence of NdFeB magnet on proper Watt- hour (Ferraris) meter behaviour is shown in the paper. It was found both positive and negative deviation, when the magnet affect braking magnet and electrical coils, respectively.

articleTitle: Modeling of a New Planar Lowpass Filter for Integrated Power Electronics Modules in Fullwave Electromagnetic Simulator
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electromagnetic filed distribution and average current density is analyzed in a new type of planar lowpass filter for Integrated Power Electronics Modules. Filter structure was proposed in paper [1]. IE3D program was used for modeling and simulating proposed structure. Results are compared with experimental data.

articleTitle: Interference Potential of PLC and Measurement of Mains Characteristics
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Power line communication (PLC) is still promoted by power distribution companies. Furthermore it is widely offered for Ethernet connections between computers and transmission of audio/video signals. Several papers showed the negative influence on the signal to noise ration of short-wave based services. This contribution exemplarily shows the significant influence on the sensitivity of a short-wave receiving station with a PLC application in the neighborhood. Besides the disturbance scenario will be examined and a measurement method will be presented to characterize the coupling loss of the mains network.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Transmission of a Sliding Wave through a Dielectric Covered Aperture
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The problem of the electromagnetic transmission trough a dielectric covered aperture in a metal screen is revisited in the context of a wave sliding along the metal surface. The problem is formulated and solved with a usual magnetic current formulation for the aperture and electric/magnetic current formulation for the dielectric. The well-known method-of-moments computational scheme is applied. Sample results are given.

articleTitle: CN Tower Lightning Current Derivative Heidler Model for the Validation of Wavelet De-Noising Algorithm
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Lightning current data collected at the CN Tower during the past 15 years need to be de-noised for precise analysis and accurate determination of the lightning return-stroke current waveform parameters. A wavelet transform algorithm has been developed for de- noising the lightning return-stroke current derivative signals measured at the CN Tower. This paper deals with the validation of the process of signal de-noising by the use of a Heidler modeled current derivative waveform. The process of the generation of a noised Heidler function will be discussed, and the results of the application of the wavelet de-noising algorithm will be presented. Different ranges of Heidler current derivative models have been generated and mixed with different noise only signals collected at the CN Tower. The application of the denoising algorithm on these noised signals has shown improvements of the SNR to up to 60 dB and correlation coefficients of up to 98 % between the Heidler models and their de-noised waveforms.

articleTitle: Issues of the Electromagnetic Compatibility between UMTS and IMT-MC Systems in the 2Ghz Band
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This article consider the issues of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) between cellular networks working in the 2GHz band and using different third generation (3G) systems, such as UMTS/WCDMA and IMT-MC/CDMA200. The main direction of this issues solution is based on analysis of the international experiences on sharing between Land Mobile networks using different standards in the frequency band of 1920-1980/ 2110-2170 MHz and analysis of ITU and CEPT documents on using this bands by 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> generation Land Mobile networks, also considered here.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulations of EMF from Dielectric Heaters and Comparative Analysis of Directive 2004/40/EC and Occupational Regulation in Poland
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The comparative analysis of various principles for limitation on workers' exposure to EMF was presented. The results of measurements and numerical calculations concerning EMF exposure from dielectric heaters were presented and used for the discussion of the consequences of various spatial averaging protocols. The obtained results have proved the practical usefulness of various calculations methods for intermediate frequency EMF exposure's assessment. For the fixed level of protection against EMF exposure, the use of the protocol of spatial averaging of incident fields in the workplace can be associated with at least 2-fold more restrictive exposure limitation taken for the assessment than with the use of protocol based on the maximum value.

articleTitle: Clarifying Scope and Definitions of the Revised EMC Directive
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The revision of the EMC Directive arose as a result of the EU Commission's program called SLIM (Simpler Legislation for the Internal Market) and of the Commission's efforts to improve legal security through a clearer and more precise text giving an answer to divergent interpretations of the actual EMC Directive 89/336/EEC. The efforts to clarify the EMC Directive were codified in an informal “Guide to the Application of the EMC Directive” released in 1997. The following year, 1998, a SLIM panel reviewed the EMC Directive and recommended its revision. The Commission published a proposal on revising the EMC Directive, which finally resulted in the new Directive 2004/108/EC. This paper will deal with the major changes brought by this revision.

articleTitle: Compatibility Analysis Method of DVB-T System Interfered with by Other Digital Wideband Systems
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Mathematical DVB-T system receiver model for the compatibility analysis with other digital systems was developed. Calculations of the protection ratios for DVB-T interfered with by other services were presented. The model can be used for calculations of the protection ratios for the interference from other wideband digital radio systems. Simulated calculations using the model were performed and the results which had been received were compared with the measurements published in the literature.

articleTitle: Regulation of RF Emissions from Power Line Communications Systems in the United States
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The United States Federal Communications Commission adopted regulations that prevent harmful interference from the radio emissions from power line communications systems. These regulations are based on limits applicable to radiated emissions, rather than conducted emissions. They do not depend solely on those limits, but also include a number of mitigation techniques, such as excluded frequency bands, excluded geographical area and consultation requirements.

articleTitle: On the Role of Plasma-Like Systems in Large-Scale Dynamics of Vortex Atmospheric Processes
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Observations, which demonstrate the important role of electromagnetic forces in dynamics of powerful atmospheric vortices, are presented. The helicity generation in the presence of plasma-like subsystems is considered. Some corollaries are discussed.

articleTitle: EMC Analysis of Pulse Transmission on a Wired Network
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electric field radiation of 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> derivative Gaussian pulses on a two-port wired network has been analyzed. Comparison of EMI from UWB pulses and that from OFDM signals of comparable data rates has been made for wired media applications. The analysis is based on computation of Radiated Field Spectral Density through PSD of signals in frequency range for wired applications. Results discussed are based on simulations and are yet to be verified by practical EMI measurements. Though the data rates considered are relatively lower for current broadband communications, the results can be used as references for EM radiation comparison between carrier-based and pulsed transmission of higher data rates on wired media.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility Tests of Warship Antitorpedo Jamming System
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents principal kinds of electromagnetic interference, which are potential source of one of warship system: antitorpedo jamming. The system is installed above and below the deck of the warships and on submarines. Such systems are susceptible to external electromagnetic noise both natural and generated by other technical sources (ships, coastline installations) and those generated on purpose (high energy microwave radiation). Selected examples of antitorpedo jamming system serve the purpose for presenting the threat and its laboratory verification. The consequences, which might arise out of lack of compatibility of such system and preventive measures were discussed.

articleTitle: Application of the Simulink to Simulation of Electromagnetic Interference on Circuits with Earth Return
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The use of a platform for multidomain simulation and model-based-design of dynamic systems Simulink permits the complex analysis of the electromagnetic interference (EMI) on earth-return circuits (ERC). In the approach presented, the ERC with excitation by A.C. signals and transients is modelled as a chain of basic circuits, which are equivalents of homogenous sections of the ERC with uniform exposure to interfering electric field. The EMI on the circuit is treated as a process constructed by Simulink as a block diagram - a graphical representation of the process, which is composed of an input, the system, and an output. The system is described by state equations, which can be solved by tools provided by Matlab. The Simulink simulation is an alternative and a useful approach to the analysis of EMI problems in ERC, when comparing with existing analytical and numerical solutions. The usefulness of the Simulink simulation has been illustrated by examples.

articleTitle: Improving the Impulse Response of Grounding Systems
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper shows that the impulsive impedance of grounding electrodes cam be significantly reduced by taking advantage of the high attenuation suffered by the high frequency components of a lightning impulse as it propagates along the grounding electrode conductors; it is shown that this effect, when combined with the shielding effect of buried metallic tubes, can lead to a considerable reduction of current surges injected into the power lines connected to these systems.

articleTitle: Spectrum Management Reform
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Is spectrum management reformation an evolution or a revolution? Over time, one or the other concept has seemed to apply. Why all the interest today in this issue, manifested by the twenty-three contributions (including plenary papers), to this Electromagnetic Compatibility Symposium's Spectrum Congestion, Spectrum Management, and Spectrum Monitoring discussions? How are management, congestion, and monitoring interrelated? Are these matters related to economic or social issues, and if so, just how important is spectrum? Where are we today with this management reform and where are we headed? What are the drivers for spectrum and why do we care? Why is spectrum management getting attention at the highest levels of politics? This paper gives certain data and explains processes relative to these questions, if not outright providing answers to them. This paper examines spectrum management at different levels, nationally and internationally. It attempts to provide insight why spectrum management today is recognized by world leaders as an important issue directly affecting large segments of the global population with declared hopes of extending its effect to literally everyone. An examination of the often intensive efforts, certainly continuing in most quarters to reform electromagnetic spectrum management, to meet societal needs, is presented.

articleTitle: FDTD-FVTD Comparisons in Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Modelling of a Mode Stirred Reverberation Chamber (MSRC) using time-domain techniques is achieved by using Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) and Finite-Volume Time-Domain (FVTD) schemes. Advantages and difficulties related to time domain simulations in MSRC are underlined in this paper. Since FDTD techniques are commonly used, number of treatments have already been integrated for MSRC studies. By allowing unstructured meshes’ design, a larger geometrical flexibility is allowed by Finite Volume (FV) method. Predicted FV numerical results are compared with those obtained by FD simulations on practical cases involving MSRC in time domain.

articleTitle: Conducted Emissions of Flyback Converter
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In small electronic devices switching power supplies are more and more popular due to their small volume, universality and price. The drawbacks are conducted and radiated emissions, generated by switching operation. Proper selection of the main elements of the converter can decrease emissions spectrum. The influence of different elements of flyback converter on conducted emissions is shown with the main point on economical solution. As the transformer is usually a custom made part, its electrical characteristics are analyzed and an optimized prototype is presented. As the results shows, the 10 dB attenuation of conducted emissions spectrum can be achieved with transformer optimization. (103 words)

articleTitle: Interferences to the 121.5 Mhz Band of the Cospas-Sarsat Satellite System in Canada
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: At the 17<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> International Wroclaw Symposium, 28-30 June 2004 [1] we presented work on the attempted identification of interferences in Canada to the 121.5 MHz band of the Cospas-Sarsat search and rescue satellite system designed to locate potential survivors of an aircraft crash or maritime distress event. At that time the interference was causing the Cospas-Sarsat system to issue false emergency reports that appeared to be in, or near, major cities in Canada. This paper presents the methodology for the characterisation of these interfering signals, examines the possible signal sources and the resolution of the 121.5 MHz interference problem.

articleTitle: 3×16 Channel Laser Driver for Optically Powered and Modulated 3-Axis Scatterers
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: MST (Modulated Scatterer Technique) is a special method of the electromagnetic field measurement characterised by very small distortions of the measured field. It allows effective applying of multi-probe version of the test setup resulting in radical acceleration of long measuring sequences. An array of 3-axis probes powered and modulated optically by means of semiconductor lasers can be used in this method. In this paper authors present a laser driver allowing simultaneous control of 3x16 lasers, designed for the calibration setup of the measuring field for susceptibility measurement purposes.

articleTitle: Radar Processing Procedures in Presence of Noise Realized on FPGA
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The target detection ability in radar can be increased using a pulse compression for linear FM signal but in radar applications several drawbacks are existed: noise, target interference and side-lobes. A standard procedure to decrease these factors is the window processing that also helps to resolve small or low power targets masked by powerful ones. In this paper we used the classical windows (Hamming, Hanning, etc.), and novel class of windows based on atomic functions (AF) theory. For comparison of different techniques the simulation and experimental radar results in presence of noise and target interference several characteristics were used, such as: coefficient of amplification, maximum level of side-lobe, width of main lobe, noise performance, etc. To implement the compression-windowing processing on hardware level it has been employed Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA). The work demonstrates the experimental results of the real time processing in a radar employing this hardware.

articleTitle: Application of the Improved MM-PO Method for Analysis of Radiating Problems
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The improved method of moments-physical optics (MM-PO) technique is presented in the paper. This method is an efficient and accurate computational tool for analysis of complex radiating structures and overcomes the well-known limitations of the conventional MM relating to the computer resources. Exemplary numerical results showing usefulness of the approach are also presented.

articleTitle: Spectrum Management in the United States --A Distributed Management Process
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes the spectrum management process in the United States, the division of responsibilities between the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) and the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA), their respective goals, organization structures, and required coordination processes.

articleTitle: 24 Ghz Ultra-Wideband Vehicular Short Range Radar Systems Technology and Regulatory Aspects Overview
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper gives an overview of the technology used for 24 GHz vehicular short range radar (SSR) devices. Based on the technical characteristics of different types of SRR available today, an impact analysis with incumbent radio services in the same frequency range is described to determine the level of harmful interference. National and international 24 GHz SRR frequency regulations that are already in force are discussed and compared with the impact study results. Finally an outlook regarding the future regulation process in other countries and the needs for a global and worldwide harmonized SRR frequency band are addressed.

articleTitle: A Picocellular UMTS/TDD Overlay on GSM System for Indoor Environment
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper a picocellular CDMA overlay on GSM system has been considered. The proposed overlay uses TDD mode of UMTS system and is designated for indoor operation in the area of macrocell of GSM system. As it turns out the implementation of overlay can significantly increase the spectrum efficiency of the frequency band that is shared by GSM system and the overlay and can provide significant capacity for overlay without degradation of GSM system performance. The picocellular UMTS/TDD overlay can be used for all the services foreseen for UMTS system.

articleTitle: The Role of Numerical Simulations in Industry Versus University
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The complexity of current EMC problems and the necessity to solve them in an accurate, reliable and efficient way require various analysis techniques. These are described in this paper with particular attention to numerical simulations as the most powerful tool for performing EMC analysis. Computational electromagnetics can be used within basic research for example at universities as well as during nearly all phases of a product or system development process occurring in industrial life. Especially here several challenges result from numerical simulations. The most important ones are described and discussed in this paper. An exemplary interference problem is presented demonstrating the relevance and impact of these challenges.

articleTitle: The Measurements Errors in Anechoic Chambers
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An anechoic chamber for measurements of antennas electrical characteristics is a closed shielded room, which walls, a floor and a ceiling are covered with an absorber. The presence of reflections from a chamber walls, floor and ceiling results in appearance of parasitic signals in a receiving point, which cause measurements errors. In the paper the errors of patterns and gains measurements of antennas with a high and weak directivity are calculated, and the methods of reduction of these errors are considered.

articleTitle: Time-Domain Analysis of Electromagnetic Field within LPS in the Case of Direct Lightning Strike
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Shielding effected by a lightning protection system (LPS) during a direct lightning strike is analyzed. Reduction of electric and magnetic fields within a zone surrounded by a LPS has been evaluated using the method of moments. The results are compared to the formulas presented in IEC/TS 61312-2 [1].

articleTitle: Schumann Resonance: Global and Local Properties of Oscillations
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Earth's surface and the lower edge of the ionosphere plasma form a spherical electromagnetic resonator. Resonance peaks are observed at frequencies of 8, 14, 20 Hz, etc. The fields originate from the global thunderstorm, and the phenomenon itself carries information on the globally averaged properties of the ionosphere and the thunderstorms. The global electromagnetic resonance is studied at a few observatories nowadays. The information accumulated is a two-fold one: it reflects the global features simultaneously with the local characteristics pertinent to the particular observatory. The report presents numerical simulations of interplay of these two qualities in the actual electromagnetic signals.

articleTitle: Simplification of the Exposure Assessment in Multiple Sources Environment
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Many reasons (economical, technical, etc.) cause that transmitting stations are equipped in many transmitting systems operating on many operating frequencies in different frequency ranges. This make difficult to assess the total exposure. This paper presents method of reduction of the number of components which have to be taken into account during the exposure assessment. Such approach substantially simplifies the exposure assessment with very little impact on assessment accuracy. In consideration derived reference levels are taken into account and far field conditions are assumed.

articleTitle: Conditions of Electromagnetic Compatibility of Narrowband and Wideband Radio Equipment: A Method of Calculation
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper we present a method for calculating the conditions necessary for elimination of interference between radio equipment when the transmitter bandwidth differs essentially from the receiver bandwidth. The method can be used for providing electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of narrowband and wideband radio equipment. Such radio equipment is finding increased usage in modern radio communication systems.

articleTitle: EMC Analysis of Broadband Pulse Antenna for Ultra-Wideband Radiocommunication System
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A complex approach to computer-aided design of the broadband pulse antenna for UWB (WPAN) communication system is presented in the paper. Investigation of the time-domain and frequency characteristics of the antenna, ultra-wideband signals and properties of the radiated field are described. Time parameters and the limitation of UWB signals’ spectrum are discussed. Results of simulation of the electric field radiated by the antenna in chosen directions are presented.

articleTitle: Radiated Emission Caused by Power-Line Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The magnetic and electric near fields caused by power-line communication were investigated. Based on a large amount of measurements, a relation between the resulting asymmetrical signals at the feed point and the radiated fields is shown. The LCL of the system is not suitable to predict the emission of the PLC-system. Therefore a different approach for testing telecommunication and powerline systems is required.

articleTitle: Hazardous Influence of Rare-Earth Magnets on Low Voltage Current Transformer as the Evidence of EMC Compatibility Lack
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper shows results obtained during research work related with influence of rare-earth permanent magnets on low voltage current transformers. This influence has the origin in the phenomenon of magnetic core B — H magnetisation which become highly nonlinear under exposure to strong stationary magnetic field. The short introduction, which outlines current situation in this area of study and justification of research work choise, are also shown in the paper.

articleTitle: Solution of MHD Evolution Equation without Resistivity in Cartesian Coordinates
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The exact general solution of the magnetohydrodynamic evolution equation for infinite conductivity is obtained in Cartesian coordinates for the case that the velocity has only one component v<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf> (x, z) which depends on the other coordinates only. Given the initial field the solution is then known at any place and time. Next one may impose boundary conditions: e.g. the value at infinity in the y-direction and/or the values at one or two plane(s), y = 0 and y = Y. One may impose other conditions too, e.g. that the field is force-free. The problem is relevant for the kinematic dynamo in astrophysics (Sun, Earth, …). The method followed is similar to the one in spherical coordinates (Callebaut, 2005), but the condition that the solution is single-valued in the azimuthal coordinate cancels here and leaves a much more general solution.

articleTitle: Frequency-Domain Analysis of Electromagnetic Field within LPS in the Case of Direct Lightning Strike
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The effect of reducing electric and magnetic fields by a lightning protection system (LPS) has been analyzed in the frequency domain using the method of moments. Characteristics of the transmittance defined as a quotient of the lightning electric or magnetic field intensity and the lightning current were investigated for the case of a direct strike. Features of the LPS shielding effectiveness were analyzed.

articleTitle: Bigarmonic Electromagnetic Wave Scattering on the Nonlinear Spherical Reflector
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper we examined nonlinear biharmonic electromagnetic (EM) field scattered on a solid sphere of nonlinear homogeneous medium and on a metal sphere, covered with medium with nonlinear characteristics. Nonlinear material constitutive equations, given as current-voltage characteristic (CVC) in the Taylor series form, are used here.

articleTitle: Automatic Verification of EMC Pulse Test Equipment by Means of the Labview Programming Environment
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The aim of this work was to create an application dedicated to the automatic verification of test equipment used in electromagnetic compatibility tests. To perform it the LabView programming environment was chosen - a versatile tool with a graphical programming language. This paper presents the normative requirements analysis, LabView environment outline and description of created software.

articleTitle: Airborne Evaluation/Verification of Antenna Patterns of Broadcasting Stations
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes a method for airborne evaluation and verification of the antenna patterns of broadcasting stations. Although it is intended for governmental institutions and broadcasters it may be also of interest to anyone who wants to evaluate large radiating structures. An airborne measurement to investigate the properties of the structure in all dimensions is needed. For complicated large transmitting arrays like multi-pattern VHF FM transmitters the accuracy offered with an airborne measurement is much higher than with any other type of “inspection”.

articleTitle: Noise Reduction Techniques Applied in EEG Multichannel System
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This article presents the design of a portable Electroencephalographic (EEG) signal monitoring system. A standard EEG registers the biological signals that have to be amplified in some thousand times, so this demands the necessity of using very low offset amplifiers and different techniques for reduction of noise interference. We also use different techniques of reducing and avoiding common mode voltages of electromagnetic interference. The 16 channels EEG system has been designed by using low power consumption circuits. We also analyze a transmission of EEG signals via Internet.

articleTitle: Considerations on Immunity Test Levels and Methods with Regard to Functional Safety
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Safety functions are more and more carried out by electrical, electronic or programmable electronic systems. Such systems are exposed to electromagnetic phenomena like they typically occur in installations and therefore the systems could potentially be affected. As a consequence a failure of the safety function could arise which might cause harm to people. Thus appropriate immunity against electromagnetic phenomena has to be achieved which is not ensured in any case by complying with normal requirements concerning electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) because they are usually derived from issues of reliability and from economic conditions. Therefore EMC and safety requirements have to be brought together. This paper describes some aspects which have to be considered when merging the topics of EMC and of complex safety-related systems. Particular attention has to be paid to appropriate immunity tests which should reflect both, firstly the potential impact of the electromagnetic phenomena on systems and equipment and secondly the need of highly reliable and accurate test results. One approach to cope with this challenge consists in the introduction of special immunity test levels and test methods in combination with a special performance criterion “Functional Safety” and if necessary by extended immunity test procedures. Furthermore the situation is discussed regarding immunity test levels and safety integrity levels.

articleTitle: EMC Standards and Regulations for PLC
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The worldwide efforts dealing with the EMC of PLC (PLT, BPL) and radio communication services are presented and discussed in this paper. The different approaches in Europe, the U.S. and Asia are described. Regulation in Europe should be based on the EMC Directive where ideally appropriate emission and immunity standards are applied. However, up to now, standardization efforts in Europe for the EMC of telecommunication networks under the EC Mandate M/313 have failed to solve the conflict between radiocommunication services and especially PLC. Probably, more flexibility from the side of the network operators will help.

articleTitle: First Experiment of Novel Electric Discharge by a Universal Electric-Cusp Type Plasma Reactor and its Possible Application to Gas Cleaning as an Electric Precipitator
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: While Magnetic Reconnection is so familiar to plasma physicists as well as geo-astro-physicists and has extensively been investigated for the past four decades on the basis of magnetohydrodynamics (MHD), there have never appeared any ideas on an electric version of field line merging reconnection surprisingly, except the author's reports. This does not mean no existence or importance of, but simply means no attention of scientists to that so far. Analogously, electric reconnection concept should be evolved, on the basis of electrohydrodynamics (EHD) for unconventional plasmas including dusty and dirty plasmas and/or aerosols that has been developed recently. When an object and/or dust grain is placed in an electric cusp region formed by an electric quadrupole, electric field line merging toward the object or grain occurs from the four poles. If the background gas pressure is beyond the breakdown threshold, object- and/or dust-related electric reconnection occurs, being followed by electric discharge. This first laboratory experiment was performed by using a universal electrics- cusp type plasma rector, This paper reports successful results, also indicating its possible use for gas cleaning as an electric precipitator among a variety of applications.

articleTitle: Licensing, Frequency Assignment and Cross Border Coordination - - Key Elements of the Spectrum Management Process
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper provides a summary of several key elements in the Spectrum Management Process. Included is an overview of the licensing process with associated procedures, a brief description of the frequency assignment process with its key goals, and cross border coordination requirements along with a current example.

articleTitle: Power Quality - An Essential Element of Today's Quality of Life
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electricity market and restructuring of the electric power sector caused that the power quality became an issue of particular importance at each voltage level of the power system. Requirements and provisions related to the electric power quality are incorporated into contracts for electric power delivery. Over the last decade the interest in this dynamically developing area of science and engineering has grown dramatically. There are many reasons for this interest, and their source is the fact, that nowadays the quality of electricity supply is determining the global economic development. It also determines the quality of life of each of us. The goal of this paper is to provide the reader with basic information regarding this domain, in the form, as it normally happens in the presence of constraints imposed by the brevity of text, distorted by the author's subjective choice.

articleTitle: Evolution of Spectrum Management Concepts
publicationTitle: 18th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Current problems of spectrum management are discussed: licensing vs. license-exempting, spectrum planning vs. flexible spectrum use, spectrum market vs. free spectrum. Focus is on the impact of new technologies and international aspects.
